card: Adds the network type to CService::GetKey() to prevent address key collisions across different networks such as Tor and I2P. Without network discrimination, per-peer address bloom filters tracking known addresses could mistake a Tor address for an I2P address sharing identical payload bytes, suppressing legitimate address announcements. A parameter preserving network-less key derivation is kept for AddrMan bucket indexing to maintain backward compatibility with existing peers.dat files.
evidence: PR description: "CService::GetKey() didn't include the network in the output. So in theory it would be possible for two IP2 and Tor addresses to have the same output from CService::GetKey(). This would have unexpected results when used in the per-peer bloom filter of known addresses - we may wrongfully assume that a peer knows foo.onion when we have sent to them foo.i2p."
Net test `tor_i2p_same_bytes` demonstrates that an I2P address and Tor address constructed with matching 32-byte payloads collide under the old `GetKey()` method.
problem: Because `CService::GetKey()` previously only serialized address bytes and port without the network identifier, addresses on different networks (such as Tor and I2P) could produce identical key bytes. When used in per-peer Bloom filters tracking known addresses during addr relay, a node could falsely believe a peer already knows an address (e.g. `foo.onion` after sending `foo.i2p`), suppressing address relay.

risk.why: A bug in address key serialization or an unexpected network enum hitting AssertUnreachable() could crash the node or corrupt address relay Bloom filters.

summary: Includes the network type in `CService::GetKey()` by default so that addresses across different networks cannot produce identical key representations. Retains an optional network-less key calculation for `AddrMan` bucket positioning to preserve compatibility with existing `peers.dat` databases.
